I've been farming these 6 mu for forty years now, and I know this land. Wheat-maize rotation is what everybody in our village does — it's what works on the plain here in Quzhou.

For the winter wheat, I'll plant Jimai 22, same improved variety my neighbor Liu uses — she got over 500 jin per mu last year. I'll sow around early October after the maize comes off. I usually put down about 50 jin of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress with urea at jointing stage — maybe 30 jin of urea per mu. That comes out to roughly 22-23 kg of nitrogen per mu. My husband says the extension people tell us to use less, but I'd rather be safe. A poor wheat harvest would hurt us badly, and fertilizer is cheaper than losing grain.

Irrigation — the well is reliable. I'll water four times: once before winter to protect the roots, then at green-up, jointing, and grain-filling. Pesticide twice usually handles aphids and the rust if it comes.

For summer maize after the wheat, I'll plant Zhengdan 958 — it's been steady for years. I'll use rotary tillage only, no deep plowing, just get the seed in fast after wheat harvest in June. Base fertilizer about 40 jin of compound, then urea topdressing at big trumpet stage, maybe 25 jin. Irrigate once or twice if July is dry. One spray for armyworm usually enough.

With only 2 of us at home and my son working in town, I can manage 6 mu myself with some hired help at harvest. Every input costs real money, so I don't waste, but I also don't skimp where it matters.
